- When sentiment is high (≥0.6), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days are below 65, forecast should not drop below 64.5 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overcorrects after short-term volatility — cap forecast at 75% of 30-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows rising trend (e.g., 0.4→0.7→0.8), model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true outcome for next 5–7 days.  
- If model forecast drops below 64 after 3 consecutive days of 65+, assume mean reversion — adjust upward by 1–3% for next 3 days.
